description: Quasar Squad is a multidisciplinary team dedicated to shaping the future of space exploration and Earth science through innovative, open-source solutions. Inspired by the vast data provided by NASA and its partner space agencies, we forge creative ideas into functional tools to solve complex global and cosmic challenges. Our mission is to bridge the gap between complex data and real-world impact, one orbit at a time.
summary: Welcome to Orbit Forge, an interactive survival and space-engineering web game where players must rely on wit, technical knowledge, and precision reflexes to survive after being stranded alone on the Moon. You're an abandoned astronaut in the surface of the Moon. Now, you need to find a way to comunicate to the Earth or the ISS. This game teaches us about the parts of a rocket, what they look like and what each part does to help in an official space mission, and thus, it helps the player to learn about how the movement and propulsion of a rocket in space with less resources and oxygen.
details:
Orbit Forge is a space exploration and survival game in which the player takes the role of an astronaut accidentally left behind by their crew at a lunar base.

With limited oxygen and no immediate way to return home, the astronaut must explore the Moon, recover the missing components of a rocket, rebuild it, and establish communication with Earth.

However, the mission goes beyond survival. Through scientific activities, logical reasoning challenges, and optional research objectives, the player contributes to space science while trying to make it home safely.

The central idea is to combine adventure, problem-solving, space exploration, and scientific education into one interactive experience

2. Main Objective and Storyline

The player begins stranded at a lunar base. The situation is urgent: oxygen is limited, the crew is gone, and the rocket is incomplete.

To escape, the astronaut must:

  1. Explore the lunar environment.
  2. Locate and collect the missing rocket components.
  3. Bring the components to the assembly platform.
  4. Assemble the rocket in the correct order.
  5. Verify that each component meets its requirements.
  6. Solve logical challenges to establish communication with Earth.
  7. Receive authorization and complete the return journey

3. Rocket Recovery and Assembly

One of the main objectives is recovering the five rocket components scattered across the Moon.

The components are:

Component

Main function

Propulsion system

Provides the thrust needed for the rocket to move

Fuel tank

Stores the rocket's propellant

Side boosters

Provide additional propulsion

Service module

Supports the spacecraft with power and oxygen

Command capsule

Houses the astronaut during the return journey

After recovering all five components, the player must assemble them on the launch platform.

But collecting the pieces is not enough. The game introduces a Build & Verify stage, in which every component must meet a specific requirement.

4. Communication with Earth

Another major part of the game is establishing communication with Earth.

The astronaut needs to solve logical reasoning challenges to restore communication channels and receive assistance.

The communication system involves space communication infrastructure, including:

  • The International Space Station (ISS).
  • NASA's mission control in Houston.
  • The Deep Space Network (DSN).

The DSN is especially important because it uses antennas located in California, Spain, and Australia to communicate with spacecraft across the Solar System.

The game transforms communication into an interactive problem-solving experience: the player must think logically to reconnect with the outside world.

Once the necessary communication is established, the astronaut can receive authorization to begin the return journey.

5. The Return Journey

Reaching the launch platform is not the end of the mission. The astronaut must complete a sequence of important flight procedures.

The return sequence includes:

  1. Engine burn: the spacecraft performs its departure maneuver.
  2. Service module separation: the service module is detached when it is no longer needed.
  3. Reentry angle: the capsule must enter Earth's atmosphere at the correct angle.
  4. Stabilization: the drogue or stabilizing parachutes help control the capsule.
  5. Main parachutes: the main parachutes slow the capsule before splashdown.

This section makes the final escape feel like a genuine space mission rather than simply reaching the end of a level.

6. Secondary Scientific Missions

One of Orbit Forge's strongest features is that the astronaut can contribute to scientific research while completing the survival mission.

There are three major secondary activities.

6.1 BioNutrients-2

This activity is based on the BioNutrients-2 experiment.

The experiment involves yeast that produces beta-carotene, exploring ways to produce nutrients during long-duration space missions.

The player must perform laboratory procedures involving:

  • Hydrating the samples.
  • Incubating them.
  • Freezing them.
  • Preparing them for return to Earth.

This activity demonstrates how biological research can support future human exploration.

6.2 CubeSat Construction

Another activity involves constructing and certifying a CubeSat.

CubeSats are small satellites commonly used for educational, technological, and scientific missions.

The project introduces several CubeSat sizes:

  • 1U
  • 3U
  • 6U

A standard 1U CubeSat measures 10 × 10 × 10 centimeters.

The game also presents the historical origins of CubeSats, their deployment systems, and NASA's CubeSat Launch Initiative (CSLI).

This activity gives players an introduction to satellite engineering and the process of preparing a small spacecraft for launch.

6.3 Lunar Rock Collection

The astronaut can also collect eight different lunar samples to contribute to scientific research.

The samples featured in the game are:

Sample

Scientific significance

Anorthosite

A light-colored rock associated with the Moon's highlands

Mare basalt

Formed by ancient lunar lava flows

Genesis Rock

An ancient anorthosite sample collected during Apollo 15

Orange soil

Volcanic glass beads discovered during Apollo 17

Big Muley

A large lunar rock collected during Apollo 16

Impact breccia

Rock formed from fragments consolidated by impacts

Icy regolith

Represents lunar soil in permanently shadowed regions where water ice may be present

Zircon crystal

Contains evidence of the Moon's ancient geological history

Collecting all eight samples represents the most scientifically ambitious version of the mission.

This creates an interesting choice: the player can prioritize a faster escape or spend additional time collecting scientific material.

7. Lunar Exploration and Environmental Hazards

The lunar environment is not just a background. It plays an important role in the gameplay.

The project introduces several characteristics and challenges associated with the Moon:

  • Extremely low gravity.
  • Almost nonexistent atmosphere.
  • Large temperature variations.
  • Lunar dust.
  • Craters and uneven terrain.
  • Meteoroid hazards.
  • The long lunar day-and-night cycle.

The player must also pay attention to oxygen consumption and seek shelter when necessary.

The game includes scientific facts about the Moon, rockets, spaceflight, the ISS, and Earth reentry. These facts appear during gameplay to connect the player's actions with real scientific knowledge.

8. Concept Maturity Levels (CML)

Orbit Forge also introduces Concept Maturity Levels based on a JPL framework.

The game presents six levels:

Cocktail Napkin

Initial Feasibility

Trade Space

Point Design

Preliminary Implementation Baseline

CDR

As the player progresses, the mission becomes more mature.

The game also introduces the idea of a checklist in which approximately 80% of the requirements must be marked green for a concept to reach a given maturity level.

At CML 3, the player must consider three possible mission strategies:

Option A — Fast & Safe

Fastest approach

Recover the five rocket components and return home directly.

Science: ★☆☆ · Cost: ★☆☆ · Risk: ★☆☆

Option B — Balanced

Recover the five components and collect at least four lunar samples.

Science: ★★☆ · Cost: ★★☆ · Risk: ★★☆

Option C — Max Science

Recover the five components, collect all eight samples, and complete the BioNutrients-2 experiment.

Science: ★★★ · Cost: ★★★ · Risk: ★★★

9. CONCLUSION

Orbit Forge is an educational space exploration and survival game in which an astronaut stranded on the Moon must rebuild a rocket, restore communication with Earth, and complete a series of scientific challenges to return home. Through lunar exploration, logical reasoning, rocket engineering, biological experiments, CubeSat construction, and geological research, players experience the challenges of space missions while contributing to scientific discovery.

Link of the GitHub Repository: https://github.com/bernardodelacerda/Orbit-Forge
